name: The she-wolf, walking north
stands_for: The she-wolf's journey out of Sonora into New Mexico (J1)
note: A pregnant wolf comes up out of the Sonoran mountains alone, crosses the Bavispe and walks north towards the line and the Animas country.
label: She-wolf, out of Sonora
credit: Traced from a Mexican wolf photograph, US Fish and Wildlife Service (public domain)
reasoning: She stands for her whole journey north; the drawing sits at her crossing of the Bavispe.

name: A steel trap with the drag
stands_for: Billy's trapline in the Peloncillos (J1 and J2)
note: Billy and his father wax their traps and set them along the trails of the Peloncillos, each on a chain that ends in a two-pronged drag buried with it.
label: Newhouse No. 4½ wolf trap
credit: Drawn after Newhouse trap catalogue engravings, 1890s-1919 (public domain)

name: The boundary obelisk
stands_for: The white boundary monuments along 31°20′ N
note: From the red hills south of the line Billy sees one of the white boundary obelisks standing alone in the desert to the east.
label: Boundary monument, 1890s line
credit: Drawn after the International Boundary Commission's monument photographs, 1892-94 (public domain)

name: The cockpit at the hacienda
stands_for: The hacienda where the wolf is made to fight (J2)
note: At a hacienda by a river near Colonia Morelos the wolf is taken from Billy and put in a pit to fight dogs at the fair.
label: Cockpit at the hacienda fair
credit: Drawn; the wolf is the traced she-wolf (US Fish and Wildlife Service photograph, public domain)

name: The ruined church
stands_for: The hermit's ruined church at Huisiachepic (J3)
note: In a ruined, nearly empty town on the upper Bavispe Billy meets an old man living in the broken church, who tells him a long tale.
label: Ruined adobe church, upper Bavispe
credit: Drawn after photographs of the Quarai mission ruin by suemruth (CC BY 2.0) and of Mission San Juan Capistrano about 1900, California Historical Society (public domain)

name: Paquimé's mud walls
stands_for: The ruins of Paquimé, beside Casas Grandes
note: The brothers ride past the old adobe ruins of Paquimé on their way into Casas Grandes.
label: Paquimé, adobe ruins, 1940s
credit: Drawn after photographs by Gary Lee Todd and DiSchamelrider (CC0)

name: The San Diego house front, L. T.
stands_for: The Hacienda de San Diego, Luis Terrazas's house (J4, J5)
note: The brothers and the girl ride up to the hacienda of San Diego, whose house front carries its name in an arch over the initials of the old owner.
label: Hacienda de San Diego, Terrazas house
credit: Drawn from the book's description; no reusable photograph found

name: The opera caravan with its gilt
stands_for: The stranded opera troupe on the Madera road (J4)
note: South of Las Varas the brothers come on the travelling opera company again, its gaudy caravan wagons halted in a field beside the road.
label: Travelling opera wagons, 1940s
credit: Drawn from the book's description; wagon form after circus wagon photographs, c. 1900-25 (public domain, CC0)

name: The blind man with his cane
stands_for: The blind man's house north of San José (J4)
note: Billy, alone, follows a light at dusk to a lone house where a blind man and his wife take him in and the man tells of his life.
label: Blind man of the revolution
credit: Drawn; hat and coat after a Fortepan photograph of a peasant with a cane (Fortepan 28839, CC BY-SA 3.0). This drawing is shared under CC BY-SA 3.0

name: The red Waco plane
stands_for: The red plane over the Babícora lake country (J7)
note: On the road towards La Boquilla Billy watches a big red Waco plane come in from the west, circle and come down beyond the lake.
label: Red Waco cabin biplane, 1930s
credit: Drawn after photographs of a Waco YKS-6 by RuthAS (CC BY 3.0) and a Waco UEC by Armchair Aviator (CC BY 2.0)

name: The gypsies' wrecked airplane
stands_for: The gypsies hauling an old airplane north on the river trail (J7)
note: On the river trail north of Corralitos Billy falls in with gypsies who are hauling the bones of an old airplane north on a cart.
label: Gypsies' airplane, lost in 1915
credit: Drawn; fuselage after a Curtiss JN-4B 3-view by Kaboldy (CC BY-SA 3.0), oxen after Giovanni Fattori's etching (CC0). This drawing is shared under CC BY-SA 3.0

name: The crippled dog
stands_for: The ruined waystation by the highway east of the Black Range (J7)
note: Sheltering from the rain in three ruined adobes by the highway, Billy drives off an old crippled dog that comes in at the door.
label: Old dog at the roadside ruin
credit: The traced she-wolf outline (US Fish and Wildlife Service, public domain), bent; the ruin drawn

name: The Trinity cloud
stands_for: The false dawn, read as the Trinity test of 16 July 1945 (J7)
note: Before daybreak Billy is woken by a great white light that floods the country and then dies away, long before the real dawn. Readers take it for the first atomic bomb, tested at the Trinity Site on 16 July 1945.
label: Trinity test, 16 July 1945
credit: Cap traced from the Trinity test photograph, US government, 1945 (public domain)
reasoning: The book names no place or event for the light. The drawing stands on the Trinity Site itself (Wikidata Q19842077), in the empty Jornada del Muerto, at the far end of the direction the dotted false-dawn line points from the waystation.
